Nothing about the responses and reprisals to Australia’s ball tampering have been proportional in a story where the truth probably lies somewhere in the middle

Who said long-form journalism is dead? As Matt Renshaw nudged his ones and twos in an already forgotten ODI match, the broadcasters were scanning Cameron Bancroft’s 4000-word essay. SEN’s Gerard Whateley was calling for a comprehensive judicial inquiry, “a little bit like a coroner’s inquest,” with witnesses compelled to attend and be subjected to cross examination. Cricket Australia’s “forum”, announced a few hours earlier, had already been skittled.

title: Sandpapergate has gone from a sporting scandal to a rolling loop of outrage and overreaction | Jonathan Horn

author: Giles Richards
description:
• FIA announces plans to recruit permanent staff

  • Lewis Hamilton has criticised inconsistency

Formula One’s governing body has announced it will bring in full-time race stewards for the first time in the sport’s history, beginning in the 2027 season.

The idea of having a select group of permanent race stewards has been under debate in the sport for some time. Currently each race has four volunteer race stewards, who change for each meeting, chosen from a pool of FIA selections, the local or regional sporting organisation and one former driver.

Continue reading...
title: F1 to bring in full-time race stewards for 2027 season in bid to end controversy

author: Stuart Goodwin
description:
• Ban by Uefa is suspended for two years

  • Uefa also fines FA £12,500 for offensive chants

England have been handed a ­suspended ­one-match ban on away ticket sales by Uefa in relation to “­racist and/or ­discriminatory” behaviour by fans at Sunday’s 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain. The punishment is suspended for two years.

Uefa has also fined the Football Association €15,000 (£12,500), with the behaviour in question believed to be the chant of “Fuck the pope and the IRA” at the ­Metropolitano ­Stadium in Madrid. A further charge in the next two years could trigger a ban on away fans for a competitive game.

Continue reading...
title: England get one-match suspended ban on away tickets for anti-pope chants in Spain

description:
Arsenal’s hopes of earning automatic progression to the Champions League quarter-finals were dashed by OL Lyonnes, as the French side continued their statement form in Europe.

Goals in either half from Jule Brand and Melchie Dumornay were the difference at Meadow Park and Lyonnes are top of the table and still yet to concede in the league phase with one game remaining.

author: By Associated Press
description:
Judge in Florida says an expert has determined the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex is mentally competent to face charges

An expert has determined that Thomas Markle, the 82-year-old estranged father of the Duchess of Sussex, is mentally competent to face charges of keeping child sexual abuse material in storage in California, a judge said Thursday.

Markle’s defense lawyer said they would not contest the finding by Dr Amie Gerodimos. The exam was ordered after his arrest at a senior care center in Lakeland, Florida, on 6 November.

Continue reading...
title: Thomas Markle, Meghan’s father, is competent to face child sex abuse images case

author: Andy Bull
description:
• Players claim brain injury caused by negligence

  • Defendants want cases to be struck out due to delays

Hundreds of former rugby players taking legal action against the game’s governing bodies face an anxious wait to learn whether their cases will be allowed to proceed towards trial. The players allege they are suffering from neurological damage caused by the professional negligence of the defendants, World Rugby, the Rugby Football Union (RFU), the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) and the Rugby Football League.

After two days of hearings at the Royal Courts of Justice the presiding judges, Senior Master Cook and Mr Justice Cotter, retired to consider whether or not the case will be able to continue in anything like its current form.

Continue reading...
title: Rugby players face anxious wait as judges consider state of concussion case

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Patrick Wintour ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Leonore Schick ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
The leaders of China, Russia and the US have held the first ever three-way talks between the three nations. President Xi Jinping likened the talks on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China, to a ‘peace summit’. Discussions appear to have focused on nuclear arms control, ending the war in Ukraine and US criticism of the international criminal court, which has an arrest warrant for Vladimir Putin. With Europe not at the table, Patrick Wintour tells Lucy Hough why the meeting is raising alarm bells in the west and beyond

Continue reading...

description:
Actors Mark Lewis Jones and Osian Morgan, who voiced characters in dub of 1977 film, among guests on red carpet

It has been a memorable few days for Wales. At the weekend, the men’s rugby team secured a historic win against New Zealand – their first victory over the All Blacks in more than 70 years. Then on Thursday evening came another culturally significant moment when Cardiff rolled out the red carpet to celebrate the first Welsh-language dub of the Star Wars franchise.

Stars of stage and screen who voiced the words of Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, C-3PO et al in Welsh (Cymraeg) over the original 1977 Star Wars film took the plaudits at the Cineworld Cardiff screening.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Welsh can tell any story’: Cymraeg dub of Star Wars premieres in Cardiff

description:
Ministry of Justice weighs video read out by Brand’s wife as Burnham urges YouTube to remove it

The prison authorities are weighing up whether Russell Brand harassed his victims by issuing comments through his wife insisting he was not guilty of rape and sexual assault.

After Andy Burnham called on Google to take down the statement from YouTube, a continuing Ministry of Justice inquiry is focusing on whether Brand has broken rules that are supposed to prevent “serious distress” to the victims of crime.

Continue reading...

• Former captain has emerged as favourite to land post

  • Aaron Finch to be appointed as coach of MI London

Adam Hollioake is being lined up for a potential return to Surrey as head coach with Aaron Finch to be appointed as coach of MI London during a winter of change at The Oval.

While Surrey are running a formal recruitment process that remains open, it is understood that the former captain is viewed internally as the favourite to replace Gareth Batty, who left after four years last month for an assistant coach’s job at the Chennai Super Kings.

title: Adam Hollioake being lined up for emotional return at Surrey as head coach

author: Robert Kitson
description:
New Zealand should provide a huge reaction to their shock defeat in Wales with enticing clash even more instructive

From the Bay of Islands on the northern tip of New Zealand to Invercargill down in the deep south, there is rare unanimity this week. Back in the day there would be parochial arguments about, say, the ratio of Aucklanders to Cantabrians in the starting XV. This time there is nationwide recognition that absolutely nothing matters beyond a bounce-back win for the boys in black on Saturday.

It is the inevitable upshot of last weekend’s seismic defeat to Wales, a result that prompted Dave Rennie, the head coach, to admit his reshuffled team had “let ourselves and our country down”. The former All Black scrum-half Justin Marshall went a step further. “We were arrogant enough to think that we could make those changes and still protect our history, and

description:
New report finds that potatoes should be able to grow on moon after they were successfully cultivated in simulated lunar soil

The humble potato could be the key to sustaining human life on the moon, according to a new scientific report asserting that prolonged lunar exploration will depend on life support systems capable of producing food there.

Potatoes are an ideal candidate for farming on the moon, scientists on a project backed by the US space agency Nasa concluded, after they succeeded in growing them in simulated lunar soil.

author: Polly Toynbee
description:
From inheritance to nepotism in the workplace, social inequality is now a daily experience for many young people

This should come as no great surprise: young people are more keenly aware of the significance of social class than those who came before them. The yawning gap in life chances at birth is something they know better than complacent older generations. Class may be unfashionable in the language of politics – long damned by the right as the politics of envy, avoided by many on the left for fear of sounding chip-on-the-shoulder – yet it’s part of the daily experience for young people.

Nearly half of 16- to 34-year-olds in the UK now say class is important to their identity – and not in a good way – according to a new Ipsos poll. That’s nearly twice as many as among the over-55s. Maybe that’s bec
title: It’s unfashionable to say it, but class still matters – and young people know that | Polly Toynbee

author: Editorial
description:
A landmark finding of genocide marked a good day for international law. But both the court and the Rohingya minority now need sustained support

The finding of the world’s highest court that Myanmar committed genocide is a landmark in international law. But at the heart of this case are “real people, real stories and a real group of human beings”, as Dawda Jallow, the Gambian justice minister, stressed in bringing it. This was one test of how the world has responded to the persecution of the mostly Muslim Rohingya minority in Rakhine state. The international community’s response to the majority judgment will be another.

This is the first time that the international court of justice (ICJ) has found a state guilty of genocide. Around 10,000 Rohingya were killed in the 2016-17 campaign by Myanmar’s military, in many cases gunned down as they
title: The Guardian view on the international court of justice: the ruling against Myanmar should be only the start for the Rohingya | Editorial

author: Editorial
description:
For almost 30 years, Grand Theft Auto has revelled in America’s vices. Its latest instalment may find room for empathy amid the mayhem

The biggest global cultural event of the year may not be something that millions of people watch together but somewhere that millions of people venture separately. In the video game Grand Theft Auto VI, players inhabit a fictionalised America through the eyes of two lovers turned cons in a rags-to-riches crime epic. On Thursday, when the game was released, workers called in sick and students skipped lectures to play at home. Such is GTA VI’s appeal that it is forecast to rake in
title: The Guardian view on Grand Theft Auto VI: a game that makes players think twice | Editorial

author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
description:
Surgeon at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary says he repeatedly voiced concerns and that patients may have died unnecessarily

A senior surgeon has called for a criminal investigation into a Scottish hospital after it emerged that at least 19 patients had died from avoidable complications due to surgery.

Dr Mohammed Habib, a consultant at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary, said he had repeatedly reported concerns about the hospital’s liver and pancreatic surgery from 2021 onwards and believed dozens of patients may have died unnecessarily there.

Continue reading...
title: Call for police to investigate Scottish hospital after 19 deaths due to surgery

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Readers respond to Alan Milburn’s plan to tackle the youth jobs crisis

Why is Labour reinventing the wheel (Alan Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people, 16 November)? There is an easier and less discriminatory way – and that is through the mainstream education system. This would not dump these young people into a post-16 Neet silo.

Further education (FE) colleges have been working in the area of young people’s training and further education for decades. Yet the sector has been continually undermined by successive governments allowing terrible salary discrimination against the FE sector and by the need to chase numbers (and cash) for A-level-type students. And why has the FE sector has not spoken up effectively for itself?
title: Here’s how we can give Neets a fighting chance | Letters

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Pam Stanier and Dr Chris Haughton on people who put up union flags and hang them upside down

It is surely ironic that the individuals who put up union flags frequently hang them upside down, as in your photo (‘Visceral response’: flag campaigns inspire anti-racism organising across England, 16 November). The broad white diagonal stripe should be at the top nearest the flagpole.

Displaying the narrow stripe uppermost is widely considered a sign of distress. Which is what I feel when I see a street sullied by the flags, whether hung correctly or not. It is an aggressive display likely to lead to disunity, not what the “union” should mean at all.
Pam Stanier
Malvern, Worcestershire
title: Another fine mess for the flag-botherers? | Letters

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Berthold Schoene responds after the head of Ofqual said students could be disqualified from GCSEs and A-levels if they tried to use AI in assessed coursework

Is this really the best we can do: draconically penalise the young for making use of the latest cognitive resources and tools available to them (Ofqual urges ‘life-altering’ penalties for students who use tech to cheat, 18 November)? Our generation has allowed the introduction of “life-altering” new technologies into every walk of life without much democratic debate, public scrutiny or governmental oversight. And now our education leaders are threatening to jeopardise young people’s career prospects for deploying these technologies within an education system that can’t cope and struggles to adapt?

We all know that AI is here to stay. And importantly, it is so much more t
title: Academic integrity matters, but students shouldn’t be penalised for using AI | Letter

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Raxa Mehta on Oxford University allowing Cofnas to give a talk on DEI, in response to an article by Ebony Riddell Bamber

As a person of Indian origin and a staunch supporter of Amnesty International and a person’s right to freedom of speech and thought, I am conflicted about my view on whether people like Nathan Cofnas should be allowed a platform or not (Oxford is platforming race baiter Nathan Cofnas. I know how corrosive that will be for Black students, 15 November).

A huge part of me wants the likes of Cofnas to be allowed to speak provided there is a fair challenge and a decent debate where their ideas are debunked smartly, articulately and intelligently based on science and facts.

Con
title: Should people like Nathan Cofnas be given a platform to express their views? Letter

author: David McKie
description:
Dashing and combative Liberal politician who was beaten to the party leadership by David Steel in the 1970s

In the autumn of 1964, the resourceful, ambitious and sometimes combative Tory MP for Finchley, north London, was challenged by a resourceful, ambitious and sometimes combative young rival who talked of seizing the seat. It was not to be; but Margaret Thatcher’s youthful opponent did halve her majority.

Political Britain would hear more of the doughty contender, John Pardoe, who has died aged 92. Yet, 15 years on, the general election triumph that swept Thatcher into government as prime minister was to terminate his parliamentary career.

Continue reading...
title: John Pardoe obituary

author: Madeleine Aggeler
description:
Experts agree that if you’re thinking of changing your diet, start small and keep your goals in mind

At this point, the environmental effects of the meat industry have been well-established: one 2021 study found that meat accounts for nearly 60% of all greenhouse gases from food production, and a 2025 report estimated that animal agriculture was responsible for 12%-19% of total human-caused greenhouse gases.

According to the United Nations, one of the best things people can do to reduce their personal carbon footprint is shift from a diet heavy in meat to one that is more plant-based. Many of us know this, but in the US and UK, fewer than 5% of adults id
title: How to start eating plant-based, without missing out on nutrients or foods you enjoy

author: Julian Borger
description:
Hailed as ‘a rare moment of justice’, judges’ decision sets out a roadmap for assessing the question of intent

The international court of justice (ICJ) verdict making Myanmar the first country in history to be found guilty of committing genocide does not just deliver justice for Rohingya victims. It also gives the 1948 genocide convention new relevance in governing the actions of nation states.

In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent.
title: Myanmar ruling gives new relevance to genocide convention and is ‘full of messages’ for Israel

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Experts say ‘insanely complex’ £100,000 limit proposed for overseas donors should be replaced by universal cap

Andy Burnham is facing calls to commit to a cap on all political donations when the elections bill is in the House of Lords, instead of the “insanely complex” £100,000 limit on overseas donors. It is uncertain whether the £72m worth of donations recently received by Reform UK will be affected.

The Labour former home secretary David Blunkett is one of many peers to have tabled an amendment calling for an overall cap, proposing a £500,000 annual limit per donor, with his plan believed to have broad support.

Continue reading...
title: Cap all political donations, not only those from overseas, Burnham told

author: Ben Eastham
description:
IMMA, Dublin
From massacre locations painted on to basalt slabs to photocollages of bulldozed airports, artists from across the Levant address their traumatic history

In 2006, Simone Fattal painted on to basalt slabs the names of places indelibly associated with massacres in the Levant since 1948: Deir Yassin; Jenin; Qana; Sabra. Through the names, in the same Arabic script, runs a line of poetry by Etel Adnan: “In our lands of drought the rain forever is made of bullets.”

Fattal’s work, which documents atrocities on a material that burst from the earth as lava before settling into stone, introduces a show that likewise combines the recording of history with anger both hot and cold.

The last named of those massacres, perpetrated by a Lebanese Christian phalangist militia during Beirut’s occupation by Israeli forces in 1982, also inspired the poem Praise for the High Shadow by Mahmoud Darwish, a line from which this show takes as its tit
title: ‘In our lands the rain is made of bullets’: Palestinian artists look back in anger, melancholy and defiance

author: Carys Afoko Lanre Bakare
description:
Pulling a sickie to play Grand Theft Auto 6? Why is there so much hype over Nathan Fielder’s latest documentary about Elizabeth Holmes ‘You Can See Everything’? What are your feelings on Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond? And have you noticed that all magazine covers look the same right now? author: Aditya Chakrabortty
description:
Milburn’s review doesn’t ask what kind of work young people will be going into: zero hours, minimum wage, mind-numbing. Do we have the guts to solve that?

One big number has been repeated over and over this week: 1 million. As ministers and journalists keep telling us, about 1 million 16- to 24-year-olds are not in education, employment or training (Neet). They’re the subject of Alan Milburn’s review, which, although not commissioned by Andy Burnham, has become the first big policy of his new government.

Rather than launch into my conclusions, let me give you three more numbers by which to judge Milburn for yourself. These figures have not appeared in any of this week’s coverage, but to understand the review’s context and its chances of success they are vital.

Aditya Chakrabortty is a Guardian columnist

Continue reading...
title: The moral panic over Neets needs to stop. The problem is bad jobs, not young people | Aditya Chakrabortty

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Sonia Exelby’s disappearance sparked an international search. The accused man, Dwain Hall, denies murdering her

Prosecutors in Ocala, Florida, have been laying out an extraordinary criminal case against Dwain C Hall, an auto repair and tow truck driver accused of kidnapping and murdering Sonia Exelby, of Portsmouth, England.

Prosecutors allege that Hall lured Exelby to the US before killing her in October last year and burying her body in a shallow grave in Marion Oaks. Hall has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Continue reading...

author: Paul MacInnes
description:
• Individual indemnity extended for potential lawsuits

  • Key figures may be named in action over Manchester City

Clubs rallied behind the Premier League’s leadership in a key vote on Thursday, overwhelmingly backing new rules that would protect the chief executive, Richard Masters, from potentially damaging lawsuits.

A vote to expand the legal indemnity afforded to Premier League directors was won 18-2 at a shareholders’ meeting in central London, granting Masters and other figures greater protection in the event they were subjected to legal action as a consequence of doing their job.

Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four Football Associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The UK bid to host the tournament is due to be ratified at an extraordinary Fifa congress in Zurich on Monday, and the Guardian has learned there is tension behind the scenes over many of Fifa’s requirements, which multiple sources involved in the discussions have indicated will not be met.

author: Jamie Grierson and Steven Morris
description:
Joanne Young, who has waived anonymity, was subjected to years of drugging and rape by former Swindon councillor, who invited other men to assault her

When Philip Young served as a Conservative party councillor for Swindon council, his contemporaries viewed him as a perfectly normal family man with “no edge to him”.

But behind closed doors he orchestrated a systematic campaign of abuse against his then wife, Joanne Young, secretly administering sedatives to render her unconscious, disoriented and amnesiac. Over a period of at least 15 years, he and other men raped and sexually assaulted her in her own bed at their home in Swindon.

Continue reading...

Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’

China, Russia and the US have said they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran triggered by two of the participants.

The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it said was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Citizens Advice criticises company for failing to meet Ofcom requirements while reporting increased revenue

Royal Mail has been accused of offering a “pot luck service” to consumers as it looks likely to miss first-class delivery targets for the fourth consecutive year.

The postal service, whose parent company was bought for £3.6bn by the Czech billionaire Daniel Křetínský last year, is meant to deliver 90% of its first-class post by the next working day and 95% of second-class post within three working days according to targets set by the regulator, Ofcom.

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Planes temporarily grounded, roads flooded and tens of thousands lose power, with evacuations in south of state

Heavy rain and high winds battered the US west coast, temporarily grounding planes at San Francisco’s airport, flooding roads in Napa county and forcing evacuations in southern California.

The fierce storm, called an atmospheric river, moved from north to south across the state. On Wednesday, San Francisco broke a rain record previously set in 1917. The city’s fire department responded to hundreds of calls, many of which related to flooding, along with downed trees and electrical wires. Flights at San Francisco airport were delayed hours because of wind.

Continue reading...
title: San Francisco breaks rain record as atmospheric river buffets California

author: Stuart Heritage
description:
It is the biggest game of the decade, but there are a billion reasons why GTA shouldn’t be adapted for television. It joins a list of wildly popular titles that won’t see the light of day on streaming platforms

You probably aren’t going to see a Grand Theft Auto TV show anytime soon. Speaking on a recent podcast, Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of the game’s parent company Take-Two Interactive, said that a film or television adaptation of GTA would only happen if its team thought that it would “somehow engage and delight our consumers. It’s a high bar to do that. And, of course, there’s always a risk of failure. So we don’t rule it out, but we’re very, very selective.”

And, well, good. There are a billion reasons why a small screen version would be a terrible idea. Creatively, the thrill of a GTA game is that no two players have the exact same experience. While you might spend your days mowing down civilians and bazookaing police helicopters out of the skies, someone else migh

Six Nations and Sanzaar executives are unhappy about Rassie Erasmus’ planned watchalong of South Africa’s Nations Championship clash against Ireland on Saturday and will consider legal action if his online show includes any television footage of the match at the Aviva Stadium.

The Springboks head coach announced he would stage an 18-plus watchalong from his Dublin hotel room rather than sit in the stands at the Aviva.

Andy Burnham due in Brussels on Friday but sticking points on food rules and tuition fees remain unresolved

With less than 24 hours to go before Andy Burnham is due in Brussels for a summit with EU leaders, the two sides still need to resolve some central sticking points, including how much of a say Britain will have in new EU food rules.

No, I didn’t watch it. I felt very sad about the whole thing because my wife and I were co-screenwriters. We went out to meet Hunter S Thompson and the poor guy was in a terrible state. description:
Òran Mór, Glasgow
In Briony Martha’s compelling play, a woman generates an alternative ending to her impromptu meeting with the Scottish superstar

We know, for example, that James McAvoy appeared in Cyrano de Bergerac at the Theatre Royal in Glasgow in the mask-wearing spring of 2022. We can also take playwright Briony Martha at her word when she says she bumped into the actor in a nearby coffee shop.

It is even true that McAvoy was in the audience of Martha’s Parasocial Activity towards the end of this summer’s run on the Edinburgh fringe: a performance that can only have had a heightened air of unreality.

Telling him would risk a lot of harm, advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith writes. If you’re going to take that gamble, you’d better be sure why you’re doing it

  • Read more Leading questions

My partner and I are engaged after a whirlwind romance, and I was over the moon when he proposed. He is a wonderful, kind and generous man, and will be an amazing husband. However, I’ve since found out that a friend I’ve known for years has always carried a torch for me, and this knowledge has made me see him in a different light. I can’t stop thinking about him, and it’s making me question if I should marry my fiance. My friend has no idea I feel this way, and has recently got engaged, so nothing has obviously changed, apart from my feelings.

Do I continue with planning my wedding and push these new feelings down, or do I tell my friend ho
title: I’m engaged but I can’t stop thinking about an old friend. Should I tell him how I feel? | Leading questions

author: Clive Paget
description:
Lott/Johnson
(Hyperion)
We lost a truly singular talent with the death of Dame Felicity Lott earlier this year. This box-set brings together some of the British soprano’s finest recordings

When Dame Felicity Lott died in May this year, the world lost a truly singular talent. An effortlessly elegant soprano, Flott, as she was known, was as at home in German, and especially French, as she was in her native English. This 10-CD boxset from Hyperion brings together some of her finest recordings from a career that spanned half a century. It’s curated by Graham Johnson, who in 1976 recruited Lott for The Songmakers’ Almanac, the pioneering vocal ensemble whose mission was to explore neglected corners of the repertoire.

First, the voice; an instrument that appears incapable of anything indecorous. It never spreads or strays from the note, maintaini
title: Flottiana album review – 10-cd collection celebrates a very, very great Dame

author: David Conn and Felicity Lawrence
description:
Failure to disclose Peter Hindmarsh’s exclusion from practice raises ‘fundamental questions’ over nurse’s case

Lucy Letby’s lawyer has said the court of appeal must urgently review her convictions, after it was revealed that a key medical witness in the prosecution’s case was barred from treating patients because of safety concerns.

The Guardian revealed this week that Prof Peter Hindmarsh – a crucial expert witness who provided an opinion at Letby’s trial that two babies had been poisoned with insulin – was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023 because his hospital considered him unsafe to treat children in relation to insulin.

Continue reading...
title: Lawyer calls for urgent review of Letby convictions after expert witness revelations

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
Leaders will wrestle with easing Brexit red tape, restoring emissions trading and opening up youth mobility

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The EU and UK will hold a long-awaited summit in Brussels on Friday – the second since Brexit – to hammer out the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc.

It will be attended by the prime minister, Andy Burnham, the head of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, and the president of the European Council, António Costa.

Continue reading...
title: What is a stake at the EU-UK summit in Brussels?

author: Guardian sport
description:
• City’s mayor says apology does not go far enough

  • Teammate admits cornerback can be ‘abrasive’

  • Ravens are on a five-game losing streak

Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey has apologized after saying Baltimore excels at “making criminals”.

The 30-year-old made the comments during an episode of his own podcast, The Marlon Humphrey Show, which was released on Wednesday. During a discussion of the city, he pointed to the Star-Spangled Banner, H&S Bakery and National Bohemian beer as things that had come out of Baltimore. He then joked: “What’s Baltimore best at making? They’re best at making criminals.”

Continue reading...
title: Ravens’ Marlon Humphrey apologizes after saying Baltimore excels at ‘making criminals’

author: Mina Holland
description:
Beaujolais is enjoying something of a renaissance, with even much-maligned nouveau gaining ground thanks to the fashion for light, chilled, low-tannin reds

“Oh, it’s beaujolais. Fantastic!” My earliest memory of beaujolais isn’t of drinking it, but of saying it, on stage, as Beverley in a school production of Mike Leigh’s Abigail’s Party. Leigh wrote the play a few years into the British craze for beaujolais nouveau, the just-made, casual quaffing wine – historically destined for local consumption in France – that’s released on the third Thursday of every November. Sold cheaply, it landed beaujolais with an image that belied its extraordinary variety and quality. It was, says The Encyclopedia of Wine, “a self-administered cataclysm” on beauj
title: How beaujolais conquered the snobs

author: Robert Reich
description:
A handful of men control the US economy. They have leveraged themselves to be – or seem – indispensable

Jensen Huang has said he would return to Nvidia as its CEO if its board requests it.

“I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

Continue reading...
title: In an authoritarian economy, Jensen Huang may be too big to fail | Robert Reich

author: Alaina Demopoulos
description:
With his unguarded lyricism and earnest delivery, the late singer-songwriter is having a moment among a generation that fetishizes unrequited desire

Sydney Tripoli has collected Jeff Buckley memorabilia since 2019. She keeps her collection of T-shirts, posters, vinyl and other merch celebrating the late singer-songwriter in what she affectionately calls her “Buckley box”. The 27-year-old scours eBay and resale sites for these pieces; lately she’s noticed the prices “skyrocket”.

“During the pandemic, it was impossible to find Jeff Buckley shirts. Now they’re everywhere on Depop,” said Tripoli, who works as an actor in Los Angeles. “Now [my collection] is worth thousands of dollars.”

Continue reading...
title: Jeff Buckley was a 90s indie darling. Now gen Z think he’s the ‘yearner final boss’

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
AI startup and Claude chatbot maker expected to become one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses

Anthropic debuts on the US stock market on Thursday after raising the largest amount of investment in history for an initial public offering.

Public trading will begin at $83 per share, higher than the expected range set last week, making the company’s fully diluted market cap $1.5tn. Anthropic announced on Wednesday that it had sold 980m shares to underwriters, an upsized offering that raised $81.3bn, surpassing the previous record set by
title: Anthropic to begin public trading at $1.5tn valuation after largest ever IPO

author: Alexis Petridis
description:
The Irish singer-songwriter would have turned 60 in early December. To mark the occasion, we revisit the best of a catalogue that’s far more than a certain Prince cover

This suitably uncompromising opener to the lengthy Faith and Courage offers a collage of radio static, Indian-inspired beats, dub bassline and whispered vocals. More importantly, it’s fantastic: you might call it trip-hop were Sinéad O’Connor’s vocal not so intense as to negate any potential for relaxation on the part of the listener.

Continue reading...
title: Nothing compares to her: Sinéad O’Connor’s 20 best songs – ranked!

author: Keza MacDonald
description:
Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids

I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “no way”. Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty.

Grand Theft Auto VI is released this we
title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child

author: Georgina Hayden
description:
Warming pie, buttery mash and plenty of gravy are a perfect excuse to gather friends around the table during chilly November

• Sign up here for our weekly food newsletter, Feast

As a Brit, there are plenty of reasons for me not to embrace Thanksgiving, most of all because it isn’t actually a British holiday, and least of all because we already have quite enough occasions to eat ourselves silly between now and January. And yet, every November, as the days grow shorter and darker and colder, I find myself rather taken with the idea of hosting a seasonal dinner for friends. If Christmas is more formal and family-focused, then Thanksgiving feels like a prime opportunity to get pals around the table, eat until you need to undo your top trouser button, and take a moment to appreciate what you have. And if that means borrowi
title: The Thanksgiving food traditions we could all share

author: Will Unwin
description:
• New head coach’s first game is at Anfield on Sunday

  • ‘We are going there with the idea to win and be brave’

Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept nerves. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and will bring those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

Continue reading...
title: Mauricio Pochettino calls for Manchester United to show no fear against Liverpool

author: Max Rushden
description:
The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly

It’s injury time at the Emirates on the 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Spurs. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and on to the post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs fans before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.

But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”.
title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Former home secretary wins 86% support in a membership vote to stand in May 2028

James Cleverly has been chosen by the Conservatives as their candidate in the next London mayoral election and says he will stand up to “anti-London” Andy Burnham.

Cleverly, who stood down as shadow communities secretary in August to focus on his mayoral ambitions, was overwhelmingly chosen in a vote of London Tory members from a three-strong shortlist, winning 86% of the ballot.

Continue reading...
title: Tories select James Cleverly as candidate for London mayor

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
Westminster joins wave of ‘job-stealing’ memes after the actor’s late success edging out the other contenders to be the new 007

Everybody is trying to get a piece of the Bond action: even the UK government.

In a post on its official Instagram account, the UK government promoted its youth jobs guarantee scheme, first announced in August, with a picture of Robert Pattinson as Bond with the joke caption: “Robert Pattinson to apply for all 90,000 jobs created for young people through Youth Employment Scheme.”

Continue reading...
title: Robert Pattinson to apply for 90,000 more jobs? UK government trolls James Bond actor

author: Matt Hughes
description:
• Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima are both standing

  • Bugt Ramon Vega fails to get the necessary backing

Fifa has confirmed that Gianni Infantino will face challenges from Philippe Diallo of France and Japan’s Kozo Tashima in March’s presidential election.

The president of the French Football Federation and honorary president of the Japan Football Association submitted nomination letters with endorsements from five member associations by Wednesday night’s midnight CET deadline. The former Switzerland and Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has not met that threshold, despite repeatedly saying he would stand.
title: Race for the Fifa presidency: lineup revealed to challenge Gianni Infantino

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Ex-minister Jess Phillips admits government does not have power to compel platforms to remove distressing content

  • UK politics live – latest updates

A new online safety act is likely to be needed to tackle convicted criminals such as Russell Brand using social media platforms to broadcast messages from prison, Labour MP Jess Phillips has said.

Just days after his conviction, Brand’s wife, Laura, broadcast a message from her husband to their 6.6 million YouTube subscribers, claiming he was not guilty of sexual offences for which he had been convicted by a jury. The video has had almost 850,000 views.
title: New law ‘may be needed’ after Google rejects call to remove Russell Brand’s YouTube prison message

author: Jane Hoskyn
description:
Save money and help the planet with these genuine discounts on everything from bamboo toilet paper to B Corp-certified bedding

• Expert tips for buying refurbished phones and laptops

Ethical and sustainable probably aren’t the first words that spring to mind when you think of Black Friday. The annual price-slashing jamboree sits cunningly in wait for your final payday before Christmas, hoping that the dangled carrot of a few quid off will make you more likely to overconsume and overspend.

Approach it with care, though, and Black Friday is a good opportunity to buy eco-friendly products that might normally stretch your budget. Many of our Filter recommendations tick either the green box or the affordable box, but we (and you, I expect) would be a lot happier if more of them ticked both.
title: Want to shop more sustainably this Black Friday? The best UK deals on eco-friendly products we love

author: Caroline Lucas
description:
Without Zack Polanski and Hannah Spencer, we might still be stuck with Keir Starmer. But after some difficult weeks, our party needs an overhaul

  • Caroline Lucas is co-chair of the cross-party campaign group Compass and a former Green MP

In the aftermath of some difficult weeks for the Greens, one encouraging response has particularly stood out for me: the widespread agreement across progressive politics that the UK is better for having a strong Green party. One that will hold other parties to account for their delivery on social and environmental justice and that will put issues on the political agenda that other parties won’t.

From Rosebank to wealth taxes and ending arms sales to Israel, Greens are stretching the Overton window so that the gap narrows between what’s necessary and what’s currently deemed politicall
title: This year, the Greens have reshaped British politics. Now we need party systems to match that influence | Caroline Lucas

author: Alex Kirshner
description:
The former NFL quarterback was widely derided when he starter his job in the Fox booth. But he has shown a human side and explains the game beautifully

I have accidentally force-fed myself Tom Brady’s commentary as my primary means of watching the NFL this season. When my favorite team, the Steelers, hired Mike McCarthy as head coach, I lodged a silent protest by declining to spend the several hundred dollars needed to get NFL Sunday Ticket. I didn’t even splurge for RedZone. That means I’ve found myself watching Fox’s NFL broadcasts on a Sunday – often an underwhelming Cowboys game – where Brady is the color commentator in the network’s No 1 booth, alongside play-by-play man Kevin Burkhardt.

This two-and-a-half-month experiment has led me to an alarming conclusion, one I’d seen others reaching gradually over the last year but never taken too seriousl
title: The unthinkable has come to pass: Tom Brady is a pretty good broadcaster

author: Lauren Almeida and Jasper Jolly
description:
Job cuts to exclude shop floor, aircraft maintenance and trainees but move prompts calls for more orders to support British defence giant

BAE Systems has announced plans to cut more than 1,000 jobs from its workforce, triggering calls for ministers to place extra orders with Britain’s biggest defence contractor.

The company said it is aiming to cut 1,070 jobs at its head office and air business in the UK, as it tries to meet customer demands for “greater speed and efficiency in getting critical capabilities into the hands of those who need them”.

Continue reading...
title: BAE to slash 1,000 jobs across head office and air business to streamline orders

author: Mark Lawson
description:
Ustinov Studio, Bath
Elliot Cowan is scarily convincing as the budding Potus in Donald, a high-speed, three-actor comedy from the playwright behind The Lehman Trilogy

His manner and actions often seeming like improbable caricature, the current US president sets a challenge for satire, any comic exaggeration likely to be trumped by reality. Mike Bartlett’s play The 47th (2022), staged between Trump’s administrations, pursued wild fantasies about the politician’s future career that were soon superseded by odder events. Ali Abbasi’s movie The Apprentice (2024) more sensibly focused on the period from 1973 to 1986 in which the New York realtor developed the behavioural and verbal tics that mak
title: Is Donald Trump beyond caricature? Not at all – here’s his hilarious origin story

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Rolling coverage of Anthropic’s IPO, and the latest economic and financial news

Those who missed out on the Anthropic IPO (or didn’t receive as many shares as they hoped) will get the chance to buy them today once trading on the Nasdaq begins.

Bloomberg reports that Anthropic’s shares are indicated to open between 20% and 26% higher in grey market trading – based on a market run by IG, and one on the crypto platform Hyperliquid.

Derivatives offered by online brokerage IG International pointed to a market value of $1.35 trillion Thursday morning in Hong Kong, implying a gain of more than 24% from the IPO price of $83. That valuation is based on the share classes sold in the deal, while the company’s fully diluted market value is roughly $1.5 trillion.

Anthropic-tied perpetual futures — contracts that

author: Sean Ingle
description:
• Three leading Kenyan distance runners all sanctioned

  • Jepchirchir also won the Olympic gold medal in Tokyo

The reigning world marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been hit with a three-year ban for EPO on a dismal day for Kenyan distance running, with two other leading distance athletes from the country also being sanctioned for doping.

The 33-year-old Jepchirchir, who won Olympic and world gold in Tokyo in 2021 and 2025 respectively, had her ban reduced by a year after she decided not to challenge the results of a blood test taken before winning the Sydney marathon in August.

Continue reading...
title: World marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir banned for three years over doping

author: Amelia Hill
description:
Swiss Cottage school for children with complex needs is place where ‘every child feels they belong’, education secretary says

For Maria, the hardest part of having a child with complex needs has been the grief: mourning the life she had imagined for her son, for her family – and coming to terms with how lonely the reality of parenting him can be.

“There are wonderful days but there are very hard ones too,” she added, tears coursing down her face.

Continue reading...
title: ‘We don’t produce Neets’: the London school recognised at World’s Best School awards

author: Lucy Mangan
description:
Julia Garner and Anthony Boyle play the FTX founders behind ‘the greatest fraud ever committed’ in the US. It’s a mind-boggling story – just make sure you don’t miss a single moment

What happens when you put really stupid clever people in charge of the world? Not as presidents (they currently trend mostly towards the merely stupid) or prime ministers (generally neither really stupid nor really clever), but in charge of the real world, which is to say the online world, the one that really governs us? We are watching that play out day by day, but if you have enough slack left in your dread-system, a cortisol spike yet to execute, why not add a warning from history to your consumption of horrors?

Welcome to The Altruists, a breakneck breakdown of the brief career of Sam Bankman-Fried (played by Anthony Boyle) who, with his on-off girlfriend Caroline Ellison (played by Julia Garner), set up the cryptocurrency exchange FTX with the belief that it would revolutionise finance
title: The Altruists review – two of TV’s best actors light up this chaotic crypto tale

author: Jonathan Liew
description:
Why do rich powerful men love golf? Ultimately the sport exists in a world where the politics is assumed to be settled

Farewell, then, LIV Golf. As its original figurehead Greg Norman once so delicately put it, albeit in a slightly different context: we’ve all made mistakes, you learn from those mistakes, and you move forward. Forward – in LIV’s case – to bankruptcy court and the start of liquidation proceedings some time in January 2027. And not without a certain irony, in the sense that Norman’s cherished project, established over a cacophony of human rights concerns, ended up getting dismembered and terminated on the orders of the Saudi government. Life moves on you pretty fast.

Perhaps the funniest part of LIV’s protracted demise – unless you count the television viewing figures – has been the last seven months, after Saudi Arabia abruptly pulled the plug on the see
title: You have to laugh at LIV’s collapse but the saga reveals money is golf’s core value | Jonathan Liew

author: Amy Raphael
description:
The actor’s latest roles see him go from a delivery guy on £40 a day to the notorious crypto scammer who stole more than $10bn. His sympathies are clear: ‘I wasn’t brought up to care about money,’ he says

In the spring of 2019, Anthony Boyle went to see Cillian Murphy in Grief Is the Thing with Feathers at St Ann’s Warehouse in Brooklyn. Afterwards, the 24-year-old actor hung around the stage door. “There were 500 people queueing up for Cillian, but I was the only one who wanted to meet Enda Walsh,” says Boyle, laughing. When the Dublin-born writer Walsh finally appeared, Boyle introduced himself. He was from west Belfast, he’d read Walsh’s plays at drama school, and it was his dream to work with him one day. He asked if Walsh would like to come and see him on Broadway, where he was playing Scorpius Malfoy, son of Draco, in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. How did he respond? Boyle grins. “He was sort of like: ‘Oh.’”

Since Walsh never went to see The Cursed Child, Boy
title: ‘Sam-Bankman Fried messaged me from prison’: rising star Anthony Boyle on playing the disgraced tech bro – and a zero-hours bike courier

author: Interviews by Georgina Lawton
description:
Mina’s substantial, aromatic workplace breakfasts and lunches are a concern for her friend and colleague Jackie. You decide who’s making a meal of the situation

• Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror

I recommended Mina as an intern but now worry as she’s always eating pungent food at her desk

Who says you can only eat simple meals in the office? It’s fun to be creative with food

Continue reading...
title: You be the judge: should my friend stop eating smelly meals at work?

author: Sarah Rendell
description:
Saracens and Canada scrum-half believes having fewer overseas players in England’s top tier would be a backwards step both for her and the wider game

Liv Apps understands only too well the benefits of playing in Premiership Women’s Rugby (PWR), so when challenging the views of the Red Roses’ head coach, John Mitchell, it comes from the heart. According to the Saracens and Canada scrum-half, limiting the international talent pool in England’s elite division would halt the growth of the game, or even dilute the PWR’s potency.

“For us Canadians, it is amazing to have the PWR because we don’t have a league at home. But then also what the Canadians and the other internationals bring to the England players, we all make each other better.”

Continue reading...
title: ‘Closing the door halts growth’: Liv Apps on PWR’s international appeal – and pruning the Red Roses

author: Jillian Ambrose
description:
Britain’s fourth-largest energy supplier brings account base up to 6m after purchase of pay-as-you-go supplier

EDF Energy will grow its share of the UK’s household energy market to more than 6m customer accounts after snapping up the pay-as-you-go supplier Utilita.

Great Britain’s fourth-largest energy supplier expects to complete the takeover early next year, adding 1.3m accounts to its customer base and taking on Utilita’s 1,500 staff. The price of the deal was undisclosed.

Continue reading...
title: EDF snaps up 1.3m more customers after Utilita takeover

author: Dominic Booth
description:
Tenth-tier club aim to become a new home for disillusioned supporters and those priced out of the Premier League

It began with a timely message on social media. “We’ve seen the posts. We’ve read the comments. If all the recent conversation has made you curious about the other team in Manchester playing in sky blue, come and see us.”

It was a direct response to the news of a guilty verdict in the Premier League’s financial fair play case against Manchester City and it came from the 10th-tier (step six) club Maine Road, who carry City’s colours and a near-identical badge, as well as the name of City’s previous home.

Continue reading...
title: Maine Road offer non-league haven to fans of scandal-hit Manchester City

author: Fiona Harvey, Graham Readfearn and Damien Gayle in Antalya
description:
Johan Rockström, one of world’s leading climate scientists, says stopping panel from working as quickly as possible is inviting disaster

Climate science is “foundational” to the Paris agreement and worldwide progress on tackling global heating, and attempts to delay new scientific reports threaten global cooperation on tackling the crisis, one of the world’s leading climate scientists has warned.

Johan Rockström, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said the world’s leading body of climate scientists, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, must be allowed to work as quickly as possible on its next comprehensive assessment of global knowledge of the climate systems.
title: IPCC report delay will threaten global effort to tackle climate crisis, says top scientist

author: Ajit Niranjan
description:
As the conference nears its final weekend, a new draft text is due to be published today, but the mood is not particularly positive

A new draft of the “cover decision” is coming this morning with little time to spare.

With just two official days left and deep divisions remaining across key priorities, including the how to address overshoot beyond the 1.5C Paris agreement targets, an electrification pledge, and the transition away from fossil fuels, the Presidencies urged Parties to lean in and move faster in a midweek update issued Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: Cop31 live: ‘Lean in and move faster’ climate summit told as deal remains elusive

author: Sarah Moss
description:
This unusual portrait of a young girl whose prison visits are interweaved with her grandmother’s war-weary reminiscences rewards attention

American author Harriet Clark’s first novel, partly inspired by her own life, is narrated by a girl whose mother is in prison. Suzanna is being raised by grandparents while her mother serves a life sentence for driving the getaway car for a botched bank robbery intended to fund revolutionary political activism. Although Suzanna refuses the narrative, in some ways this is a coming-of-age story, but with a protagonist whose overwhelming need is to go nowhere and change nothing.

The Hill is shaped by the tension between the novel’s need for a plot and Suzanna’s rejection of her own role in the Bildungsroman. Prison visits structure Suzanna’s life, their rituals and repetitions at once marking and resisting the passage of time. At first, her grandfather drives her from their shabby urban apartment to the hilltop
title: The Hill by Harriet Clark review – distinctive debut of growing up with a mother in prison

author: Guardian Staff
description:
If there was a rave going off in the 90s, one British photographer was likely there with his camera. His new book celebrates banging nights out at Cream, the Haçienda and more

Continue reading...
title: Bet they look good on the dancefloor: Mark McNulty’s party people – in pictures

author: Lola Okolosie
description:
I welcome Alan Milburn’s call for schools to focus more on students’ potential beyond exams. Yet I must ask: where is the money?

At 16, life should feel like a path leading to endless opportunities. That is at least the carrot dangled in front of young people to motivate them through the gruelling years of exam preparation. “Your life starts now,” their teachers all but tell them. And though for the vast majority that is true, there is a cohort who are forced to accept that the bright futures they were promised are beyond their reach. They are the nearly one million young people aged between 16 and 24 who are not in education, employment or training (Neets).

Alan Milburn’s second report on the nation’s Neets places schools at the heart of the solution. It proposes that schools should be judged not only on grades but also whether pup
title: Teachers want to prepare pupils for post-16 life. This is why it’s so difficult | Lola Okolosie

author: Rose Shepherd
description:
As the new Good Hotel Guide goes live online, the editors pick their favourite places to stay for hikers and strollers

With stunning views over Borrowdale, Donna and Gary MacRae’s small country house hotel is in a walker’s wonderland, with routes for all abilities, from the challenge of a Wainwright to a stroll around the wooded grounds. Donna and Gary can supply a packed lunch, arrange for a mountain guide and share information on favourite walks. For Gary, that means a scenic, “easy-going stroll” from Dock Tarn to Watendlath National Trust village and tarn; for Donna, a hike to the top of Rigg Head Quarry, then on towards High Spy, along the river over Maiden Moor and Catbells. Drying facilities, drinks and canapes and a four-course dinner await the rovers’ return.
Doubles from £200 B&B (2-night min), dinner from £55pp, no pets, no under 15s, hazelbankhotel.co.uk
title: Walk, eat, sleep: 10 of the best hotels for ramblers in the UK and Ireland

author: Reuters
description:
Awami League party called for ⁠nationwide protest on Thursday after the government rejected Hasina’s request for passport

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down Thursday as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home ⁠of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.

Hasina’s Awami League party had called for a ​week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support ‌for Hasina’s planned return in December, culminating in a ‌nationwide lockdown on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Violent protests and killings in Bangladesh ahead of exiled Sheikh Hasina’s planned return

author: Phil Harrison, Jack Seale, Ali Catterall, Hollie Richardson and Hannah Verdier
description:
Harrowing accounts of the Hanukah celebration attack in Sydney last December. Plus: Marci Pierre White and Gordon Ramsay reunite. Here’s what to watch this evening

10pm, Channel 4
This harrowing documentary recalls the events of 14 December 2025 when terrorists attacked a Hanukah celebration taking place in Sydney. It’s also a celebration of the courage of the first responders – and of the many people who put their own lives on the line to save those under attack. The survivor testimony and the attack footage make it a difficult watch but it’s a striking one, too. Phil Harrison

Continue reading...
title: TV tonight: survivors from the Bondi beach terror attack share their stories

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Modelling in draft of 10-year London plan threatens Sadiq Khan’s promises on improving air quality

Car use in London will rise by 10% over the next decade with cycling and walking falling as a proportion of trips, according to an official forecast by the city’s mayoralty, putting into doubt Sadiq Khan’s promises on air quality and the environment.

Based on projections in the draft version of the latest 10-year London plan, drawn up by the mayor’s office and Transport for London (TfL), road congestion from a growing population would slow buses down, while packed tube services might require stations to close regularly to ease numbers.

Continue reading...
title: Car use in London forecast to rise by 10% in next decade

author: Rachel Roddy
description:
Much like tomato, the plum has a natural acidity and sweetness that works brilliantly in a delightfully jammy pasta sauce

Standing on platform 2 at Baker Street station a few weeks ago, a grey creature scuttled under the raised tracks. “You’re never more than six feet away from a rat in London,” I said to my Roman son. “It’s a mouse, Mum,” was his hardboiled reply to my rehashing of an urban myth. A myth that turns out to be inaccurate, according to Dr David Cowan, whose research on the subject resulted in estimates of anything from 10ft-164ft: in other words, while it’s impossible to know for sure, in certain areas you might be very close to a rat.

The same can be said about wild plum trees all over the world. While it’s impossible to know exactly, even in dense urban areas, you might be very close to a wild plum tree or, more correctly, a cultivated plum that has gone fera
title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for pasta all’arrabbiata with red onion and plums | A kitchen in Rome

author: Martin Belam and Miatta Mbriwa
description:
Test yourself on topical news trivia, pop culture and general knowledge every Thursday. How will you fare?

The Thursday quiz spent the weekend up in Inverness where it was unexpectedly blinded by winter sunshine and met an awful lot of European herring gulls, including one particular persistent young chick that was quite adamant passersby should be feeding it. It clearly could not read the signs.

Anyway, now is your opportunity to show you can read the signs, or at least read 15 questions on topical news, general knowledge and popular culture. There are no prizes except potentially a warm feeling inside. A considerably warmer feeling than Inverness at this time of year, at any rate. Allons-y!

Continue reading...
title: Thursday news quiz: A hungry hippo, a distant Voyager and a new James Bond

author: Phillip Inman
description:
UK central bank will want to avoid echoes of expensive US Federal Reserve revamp that led to Trump clash

Andrew Bailey may spend his days closely watching developments in the strait of Hormuz or US stock markets for signs of shocks to the global economy – but the Bank of England’s governor has a £160m problem brewing much closer to home.

A secretive major revamp of the Bank’s historic headquarters in the heart of London’s Square Mile presents a huge test of Bailey’s project management skills. The central bank, with its reputation staked on carefully counting the nation’s pennies, will be keen to avoid delays, budget-busting or any echoes of the expensive US Federal Reserve revamp that left his former peer Jerome Powell awkwardly clashing with Donald Trump on camera.
title: Grade I interiors, gold bars, cost fears: Bank of England faces headache over £160m revamp

author: George Monbiot
description:
The government doesn’t know what they are going to be used for, but that’s beside the point. Their real purpose is to sustain the share price of big tech

It should have the status of an economic law: the sectors a government does most to promote in the name of growth are the sectors most likely to tank the economy. In the UK and the US, deregulation was meant to turn the financial sector into a never-ending growth machine. We have not yet fully recovered from the crash it helped cause in 2008. Fossil fuels are the most heavily subsidised sector on Earth. All that public money makes us highly vulnerable to oil price shocks, the whims of autocrats and societal collapse caused by climate breakdown. As for the great growth priority of our time – AI and datacentres – well, don’t take it fro
title: Ram through datacentres no one wants and hope the AI bubble never bursts: that’s the UK’s growth plan | George Monbiot

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Former minister, who was sentenced to prison in Bangladesh in her absence, says she was victim of ‘malicious prosecution’

The former minister Tulip Siddiq has said she is considering taking legal action against the former interim leader of Bangladesh over corruption allegations made by his administration led her to resign from the UK government last year.

The MP for Hampstead and Highgate, whose aunt Sheikh Hasina was put on trial in absentia over crimes against humanity during her 15 years as prime minister of Bangladesh, was accused of benefiting from the former regime by the authorities in the Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka.

Continue reading...
title: Tulip Siddiq says she is considering legal action against former Bangladesh leader

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
A poll of more than 40,000 workers found that a better work-life balance was the main reason people consider leaving their jobs

Work-life balance has become the leading reason why workers consider leaving their jobs, according to a new global workforce survey, as flexibility is valued more than a higher salary despite the cost of living crisis.

A poll of more than 40,000 global workers found that the top reasons for seeking a new role were better balance between professional and private lives, more flexibility over working schedules or remote working opportunities.

Continue reading...
title: Flexibility more important to jobseekers than pay, global survey finds

author: Virginia Spiers
description:
Tamar Valley, Cornwall: In the autumn warmth, the river brings flotsam and Canada geese, while a group of vintage Austin car enthusiasts have a picnic

By Cotehele quay, on the last of a sequence of calm sunlit days, thin plumes of mist rise from glistening mudbanks and reedbeds glow luminous in the morning sun. Gig crews drag their boats up the slipway, away from the ebbing water. Lime-loving old man’s beard on riverside bushes reminds us of the cargoes of limestone, once shipped with coal to these quays for burning in the monumental kilns.

Upriver, the woodland path towards the river cliff chapel is strewn with dry leaves, and beech and sweet chestnut hang on to green and golden foliage. The National Trust’s valley garden remains in shade, apart from the fiery top of a
title: Country diary: A luminous morning of gig crews and green and gold foliage | Virginia Spiers

author: Patrick Barkham
description:
Scientists use lightweight tracker to map wading bird’s extraordinary migration from Norfolk to the Arctic and back

A bar-tailed godwit called Phil has completed a 6,800-mile journey from Norfolk to Siberia and back again, in the first mapping of the endurance feats of this long-distance migrant.

A wading bird not much larger than a pigeon, the bar-tailed godwit is known for making the longest recorded non-stop migratory flight of any bird, with populations that visit Britain spending summers breeding in the Arctic Circle before retreating to the unfrozen wetlands of Britain in winter.

Continue reading...
title: Meet Phil, the bar-tailed godwit tracked on a 6,800-mile round trip to Siberia

author: Stuart McGurk
description:
Slap fighting is the world’s newest combat sport. Built for short attention spans and super-viral moments, it’s aiming for global dominance. No flinching

In the days before Power Slap 22, in Belgrade, Serbia, in late July, the organisers of the world’s newest combat sport were taking no chances. At the Crowne Plaza hotel, where competitors were booked to stay, those facing off had been separated by floor, lest any unauthorised violence took place.

It turned out there was little need. The night before the main event, contestants mingled amiably in the lobby and bar. The atmosphere was more specialist sales conference than brewing barroom brawl. In the lobby, I joined Louis “Razor” Robinson, and Ryan “the Punisher” Kenny. “We’re all friends in slap,” Robinson said, earnestly, by way of a greeting. Robinson, a Brit from Stalybridge, Greater Manchester, is 30, stout, intense. Kenny, a Canadian, is 34, lofty, laid back.
title: Nothing but highlights: is Power Slap the sport we deserve?

author: Charlotte Higgins
description:
The more you gaze at ​these 10 surviving works, ​with their cryptic inscriptions and even fool’s gold, the more the Flemish master trips you up​ – but being laughed at like this is all part of the glorious pleasure

  • Van Eyck: The Portraits review – a jewel box of phenomenal death-defeating paintings

At the Barbican Art Gallery in London, there is an exhibition of some of the white paintings made by the US artist Robert Ryman over 60 years from the 1950s. The paintings are square, because a square is neutral, and he didn’t want viewers associating them with the visual language of landscape or portrait. For Ryman, his paintings resolutely were what they were, which is to say, white paint applied to
title: Tricks! Traps! Riddles! Jan van Eyck’s portraits look vividly real – but are full of secret messages. What do they mean?

author: David Jays
description:
Wales Millennium Centre, Cardiff
Sheen is in wondrous voice as Owain Glyndŵr, clashing with Henry IV, in Gary Owen’s stirring history play for Welsh National Theatre

No one does rousing like Michael Sheen. Whether urging on the Welsh World Cup squad or vowing “apocalypse” on The Traitors, he surges forward on waves of rhetoric. As Owain Glyndŵr, beacon of Welsh resistance, he doesn’t disappoint. “We can die gently and be forgotten,” he exhorts his followers. “Or we can rage.”

Rage and resignation, the sword and the song, resonate through Gary Owen’s absorbing medieval epic for Wales Millennium Centre and Sheen’s new Welsh National Theatre. Glyndŵr is a marginal figure in Shakespeare’s Henry IV plays, a thorn in the unstable king’s side. Here he stands central, a fitting protagonist for a moment of both surging populist politics and
title: ‘We can rage’: Michael Sheen fires up the gripping medieval epic Owain & Henry

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
About 2.6m adults are taking the drugs, fuelled by the regulator’s approval of the pill versions and a rise in male users

At least one person is taking weight-loss drugs in 8.5% of households in Great Britain, according to research, meaning there are more homes with GLP-1 users than those containing vegetarians and pescatarians combined.

About 2.6 million adults were using weight-loss medication in August, a rise of about 700,000 people since February, according to a survey by Worldpanel by Numerator.

Continue reading...
title: Weight-loss drugs used in nearly one in 10 homes in Great Britain, study finds

author: Joël Reland
description:
In laying a trap for himself, the PM could derail his longer-term ambition of revisiting Brexit

This week’s UK-EU summit may, one day, be seen as the start of the UK’s long march back towards the EU. Andy Burnham’s much-anticipated first meeting with EU chiefs in Brussels on Friday will be used to unveil a suite of detailed agreements to improve trade and economic cooperation, before the Prime Minister kickstarts his longer term “national conversation” about a much closer form of political and economic relationship with the EU. This, as Burnham signalled in a speech on Monday night, could well culminate in Labour’s next election manifesto abandoning the party’s famous red lines, and proposing an application
title: Andy Burnham is in danger of over-selling his big Brussels summit. What happens if he under-delivers? | Joël Reland

author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
description:
Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas

The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth.

Continue reading...
title: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns

author: Rosemary Behan
description:
Like Russell Brand, my father was put on a pedestal by the media, despite a history of troubling, misogynistic comments. Meanwhile, my mother suffered through years of appalling treatment

Even though decades have passed, part of me feels I should not be telling this story. Not because it isn’t true, but because telling makes it real. And the reality is very hard to bear.

I was a young child at home in Whitechapel, east London, when my mother came into my bedroom, which was next to my parents’, and told me that my father had raped her. He had gone off to work and I was too young to fully understand what the words meant – perhaps seven or eight – and I remember being angry with her for upsetting life again, as she had done before, when she suddenly came to me at the top of the stairs and told me that they would “have to part” and that would mean taking me away with her.
title: ‘I came close to killing Sally about six times’: how my abusive father was enabled by his fame

author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
description:
Reviewers praise relationship between two leads in hotly anticipated release, whose trailer attracted 90m views in 24 hours

Good things clearly come to those who wait. After 13 years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here – and, according to critics, it’s a masterpiece.

The trailer for the video game, which returns players to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, attracted more than 90m views in 24 hours when it was released in December 2023. Excitement continued to mount, with two release delays and a steady stream of leaks and speculation keeping the game in the headlines.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Most extraordinary virtual world’: critics hail Grand Theft Auto VI as masterpiece

author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Jessica Elgot and David McAllister; produced by Eleanor Biggs, Alex Atack, Harriet Mogie and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
description:
Deputy political editor Jessica Elgot and influential MEP David McAllister on the prospect of the UK rejoining the European Union, before Friday’s UK-EU summit

On Friday, Andy Burnham will be in Brussels, to sign off a series of new deals between the UK and the EU.

The prime minister claims the deals – covering areas from food to youth mobility to carbon emissions – will boost UK GDP by £17bn.

Continue reading...
title: Brejoin? Is Andy Burnham going to reverse Brexit? – podcast

description:
Leaders of the US, China and Russia to take part in their first trilateral, with developments on trade, AI and global conflicts closely watched

  • Xi Jinping rallies against protectionism as he welcomes Trump to Apec summit

  • What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds

The Guardian’s correspondent Rebecca Bailey is in Shenzhen, where she is covering the events of the day.

Describing the mood on the ground and what we can expect today, she writes:

title: Apec summit live: Xi, Trump and Putin set to hold historic trilateral in China

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Bayesian, which sank off Sicily killing seven including tech tycoon, had not been fully assessed, say investigators

The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said.

The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when it sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Mike Lynch’s superyacht had unidentified vulnerability to high winds, report finds
